8d2d4525486671544cdb8a9f6328177430410204.summary: Hunt.io analysed three exposed open directories of an active intrusion crew. Hospital staff credentials and a VPN session are reported in operator hands, though their validity is not established. A US manufacturer's cloud storage was listed with a live token. US law firms and federal agencies are targeted; one firm faces sustained attacks but no breach is confirmed. Tooling includes a malicious JDBC provider chaining to an Apollo-derived Windows payload and a Poseidon Linux implant. The attribution is an assessment only: a Chinese-speaking, Southeast Asia-based cybercrime operation.

hedges: Named law firms and agencies were targeted or enumerated, not compromised by this operator, unless marked as confirmed.
Attribution is an assessment drawn from indicators in the files, not a validated attribution; no named group is tied.
Hospital credential material is not shown to be a proven domain login or patient-data loss; its validity is not established.
Cloud storage was listed, not downloaded, and the SAS token was not tested.
Hash-candidate generation does not establish successful cracking or access to an on-premises domain.
For Simpson Thacher, all captured credential-stuffing and exploit results show failure; no evidence the firm was breached.
Payload and implant artifacts were read statically; no sample was executed and a live implant callback is not shown.
Infrastructure associations listed by the platform are not proof of common ownership.
